column3: The Hebrew says it becomes a skin-disease lesion, rather than “could become” one, and repeats “the skin of his flesh.”
The Hebrew retains the image “in his eyes” for the priest’s observation.
The Hebrew says he shall not isolate him, rather than merely that he need not do so.
The Hebrew explicitly names the priest’s eyes and repeats the skin disease as the covering agent.
The healing is expressed passively: the boil is healed.
The Hebrew says the spot stands in its place, rather than simply remains unchanged.
The Hebrew says the spot stands in its place and does not separately add “only” before the scar.
The Hebrew names the beard rather than the chin.
